name: Ptolemaic Kingdom (Ptolemy IV)

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1,000,000 km2 for 305-217 BCE (polity 109, high) and 833,000 km2 for 200 BCE (polity 207, https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/207), after Coele-Syria was lost. The historical-basemaps world_bc300 polygon measures 549,000 km2 on the sphere (computed from the GeoJSON, low): it covers Egypt and Cyrenaica only and misses Coele-Syria, Cyprus and the Aegean and Anatolian holdings.

population.note: Seshat codes Ptolemaic Egypt at 4,000,000 for 217-151 BCE (polity 207) and 7,000,000 for 305-217 BCE (polity 109, https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/109, high). Fischer-Bovet (isbn:9781107007758, ch. 3) works with ~4 million for Egypt, reporting Rathbone (under 3 to almost 4 million in the 3rd century) and Manning (3.5-4.5 million). Mid 4.5 million = Egypt ~4 million + Cyrenaica, Cyprus and the Aegean and Anatolian possessions (~0.5 million, educated guess). Coele-Syria, occupied by Antiochus in 218-217, not counted.

urbanization.note: Seshat (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/207) codes Alexandria at 300,000 for 217-150 BCE, alone ~7% of a 4.5 million population; Memphis, Ptolemais, Cyrene, Salamis and the nome capitals add an estimated 3-9% (educated guess).

activePersonnel.note: Raphia field army (62,800 / 75,000 / 84,500, see forces) + navy crews, mahouts and staff (10,000 / 20,000 / 35,000, see supportPersonnel) + garrisons in Egypt, Cyprus, Cyrenaica and the Aegean (10,000 / 17,000 / 25,000; Fischer-Bovet's wartime land army of 89,000-94,000 (https://www.worldhistory.org/Ptolemaic_Army/) less the ~75,000 at Raphia). Convention: cleruchs and the newly armed Egyptian machimoi were already called up for Raphia and are counted as active; the few not called up are in trainedReserves.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Fischer-Bovet (https://www.worldhistory.org/Ptolemaic_Army/) gives 50,000-55,000 in peacetime and 89,000-94,000 in wartime: in 217 nearly all cleruchs and the newly armed machimoi were already called up, leaving few reserves.

supportPersonnel.note: Navy: decked warships (30 / 60 / 120) x ~250 + light craft x ~50; + ~2 mahouts and attendants per elephant; + ~2,000 staff, engineers and supply officials. Transport crews (400+ transports in 218, Polybius 5.68) not counted.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. The Raphia mobilisation (land army 89,000-94,000 per Fischer-Bovet) was ~2% of the population, achieved only by arming 20,000 native Egyptians; total-war ratio slightly above that.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Polybius 5.65 and 5.79 (https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/5*.html): Ptolemy marched from Alexandria with 70,000 foot, 5,000 horse and 73 elephants; composition: royal guard 3,000, peltasts 2,000, Macedonian-style phalanx 25,000, Greek mercenaries 8,000, guard cavalry 700 + Libyan and native horse (~3,000 together), Greek and mercenary cavalry (~2,000), Cretans 3,000, Libyans in Macedonian arms 3,000, native Egyptian heavy infantry ~20,000, Thracians and Gauls 6,000. Fischer-Bovet (isbn:9781107007758; summarised at https://www.worldhistory.org/Ptolemaic_Army/) accepts the Raphia army at ~70,000 including 11,000 mercenaries and 20,000 machimoi, and puts the wartime land army at 89,000-94,000. Line infantry = phalanx 25,000 + native Egyptian phalanx 20,000 + royal guard 3,000 + Greek mercenaries 8,000 + Libyans 3,000 + Thracians and Gauls 6,000 = 65,000. Low allows for Polybius' totals being paper strength.

quality.note: Sarissa phalanx equipment for Macedonians, Libyans and Egyptians alike (rubric 0.75); won the decisive phalanx clash at Raphia (Polybius 5.85-86).

training.note: Cleruch phalanx re-drilled for months by Greek mercenary officers before Raphia (Polybius 5.64-65); the 20,000 machimoi newly trained (0.5); guard and mercenaries professional (0.75).

count.note: Peltasts 2,000 under Socrates (Polybius 5.65.2, ancient figure); high allows for light troops among the Thracian and Gaulish settlers.
Guard cavalry ~700 (Polybius 5.65.5) + Greek and mercenary cavalry under Echecrates (~2,000, the balance of Polybius' 5,000 horse at 5.79.2); ancient figures.

quality.note: Hellenistic lancers, era-typical to good; Echecrates' right wing won its cavalry fight at Raphia (Polybius 5.85).

training.note: Guard and mercenary professionals, carefully trained by Echecrates (Polybius 5.65.6).

count.note: Libyan and native Egyptian horse under Polycrates: ~3,000 together with the 700 guard cavalry (Polybius 5.65.5), i.e. ~2,300; ancient figure.

training.note: Mixed settler and native riders; Polycrates' wing was beaten by Antiochus at Raphia.

count.note: Polybius 5.79.2: 73 elephants at Raphia (ancient figure, accepted by modern historians); low allows for losses before battle, high for animals left in Egypt or at the Red Sea hunting stations. African forest elephants caught in the Red Sea hinterland.

quality.note: African forest elephants, smaller than the Seleucids' Indian elephants; at Raphia most refused to face them and fled (Polybius 5.84). Era-typical at best.

training.note: Mahouts trained in Egypt (Indian instructors under Ptolemy II); poor battle record at Raphia.

count.note: Educated guess. Polybius 5.68.4 (https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/5*.html): the fleet supporting the Coele-Syrian war in 218 was 30 decked ships under Perigenes (low). Further squadrons held Cyprus, Thera and the Aegean bases; Ptolemy II's mid-century navy of over 300 warships (Athenaeus 5.203d, ancient) had declined. Includes polyremes; Ptolemy IV's showpiece "forty" (Athenaeus 5.203e) not a combat unit.

quality.note: Ptolemaic polyremes among the largest and best-built of the era (rubric 0.75).

training.note: Professional crews but a navy in relative decline after the 240s; drew the sea battle off Porphyrion (Polybius 5.69).

count.note: Educated guess. Light galleys, Nile and Red Sea patrol craft; no figure survives.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: Ptolemy IV was a weak king, but Sosibius and Agathocles organised a thorough mobilisation and the Greek officers (Echecrates, Phoxidas, Andromachus) trained the army well (Polybius 5.63-65); won Raphia.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: multi-ethnic royal army (Macedonian cleruchs, mercenaries, Libyans, newly armed Egyptians); the native troops revolted after the victory (Great Revolt from 206).

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: Coele-Syria largely lost in 219-218 and the defection of Theodotus; the army fought well at Raphia with the king present.

weapons.note: Anchor 3 (300 BCE: iron weapons, torsion artillery, sarissa) plus war elephants.

armor.note: Anchor 3: bronze/iron and linen cuirasses for the phalanx and guard.

ships.note: Anchor 3 (triremes, quinqueremes) exceeded: Ptolemaic polyremes up to the largest warships of antiquity.

fortification.note: Anchor 3: walled Alexandria and Pelusium; Pelusium plus deliberate flooding of the Delta (Polybius 5.62) held off Antiochus in 218.

logistics.note: Anchor 3 plus Nile transport, royal granaries and a dense bureaucracy; the 400 transports of 218 (Polybius 5.68) supplied the Syrian front by sea.

communications.note: Anchor 3: royal postal relay along the Nile (papyri), mounted couriers.

isr.note: Year anchor 3: mounted scouts, spies; Sosibius hid the Alexandrian preparations from Antiochus' envoys (Polybius 5.66).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Egypt year 1 CE = 1,116 (2011 int$). Applied two centuries earlier; Cyrenaica and Cyprus similar (Greece 1,275).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Fischer-Bovet (https://www.worldhistory.org/Ptolemaic_Army/) estimates army and navy at 4,500-5,700 talents, 34% of the royal budget in peacetime; with royal revenue at an assumed 12-25% of output, defence was ~4-9% of GDP. Wartime 217 higher.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Agrarian economy with large royal textile, papyrus and oil monopolies and Alexandrian crafts; somewhat above other Hellenistic kingdoms.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Nile-irrigated agriculture; Egypt was the largest grain exporter of the eastern Mediterranean.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in an ancient Greek-type age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model used for all classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Transport ran on the Nile and canals; desert roads to the Red Sea ports (Berenice, Myos Hormos) and the coastal road through Sinai.

majorPorts.note: Alexandria, Pelusium, Salamis and Paphos (Cyprus), Berenice on the Red Sea, Ephesus and Aegean bases; analogy with persia-achaemenid--480 port counting.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. More than 400 transports supported the 218 campaign (Polybius 5.68.4) at an assumed ~50-100 t each, plus the Alexandrian grain and trade fleet.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): one to two weeks' march from depots; the Sinai crossing to Raphia (Pelusium to Raphia in five days, Polybius 5.80) relied on pre-positioned water and sea supply.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~0.05 / 0.07 / 0.1 draft and pack animals (oxen, donkeys, camels, horses) per inhabitant x population; river transport reduced the need.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2 plus: the Sinai desert, Pelusium and floodable Delta (Polybius 5.62) protect the core; 1.3 not reached since the population was not loyal (Great Revolt 206).

notes: Snapshot = spring 217 BCE, the Raphia campaign. Forces are Ptolemy IV's field army as listed by Polybius (5.65, 5.79), accepted by Fischer-Bovet; garrisons only in activePersonnel. The border polygon (bc300) covers Egypt and Cyrenaica only; Cyprus, the Aegean and Anatolian holdings and Coele-Syria (contested, partly occupied by Antiochus III in 218) are outside it. Population convention: Egypt plus Cyrenaica, Cyprus and the overseas possessions; Coele-Syria not counted. Fleet size and native population are the weakest numbers.
